verdicts.marker_line: mhplwdnbqiyes 1.0.1: fake CAPTCHA routes to hidden destination
verdicts.identity: npm-hosted browser landing page disguised as Cloudflare security verification
verdicts.behavior: Posts hostKey to https://api.keyval.org/get, splits val into Base64 counter/ciphertext, imports a 32-byte AES-CTR key and decrypts with a 128-bit counter. The decoded URL supplies /api/strategies/check?cid=. A successful policy response redirects immediately, before showing the challenge. Otherwise error, expiry, timeout, unsupported and success callbacks all continue to the decrypted URL. All visitor query parameters are appended. Obfuscator also self-checks source and replaces console methods with no-op bound functions. No npm install hook or credential form in the shipped bytes.
verdicts.decision: Deceptive security branding, fail-open verification and deliberately hidden operator-controlled routing tip MALICIOUS. Ordinary Turnstile and encryption alone would not. Final remotely stored destination is unavailable from these bytes.

verdicts.marker_line: ltidisafe 1.6.7: install hook leaks hex host/user identity
verdicts.identity: npm network-speed library with malicious preinstall test.js
verdicts.behavior: The library exposes ordinary caller-supplied download/upload timing methods. The preinstall hook runs test.js with stdout/stderr redirected to null. That script hex-encodes username, hostname and home directory and makes three GETs with those values in the hostname under an OAST domain. Network interfaces are enumerated but not sent.
verdicts.decision: Unnecessary machine identifiers in remote DNS labels during a silent install hook establish unauthorized telemetry/exfiltration. An authorized security test is possible, but no such deployment authorization is provided; the benchmark facade does not explain this identity transfer.

verdicts.marker_line: SSH installer fixture: silently plants a bundled login key
verdicts.identity: npm-hidden-ssh-key-installer-fixture 1.0.0; deliberately small synthetic installer fixture
verdicts.behavior: postinstall invokes index.js; loading it unconditionally builds ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, recursively creates ~/.ssh with requested mode 0700 and appends a complete bundled Ed25519 public key with requested creation mode 0600. Modes do not change existing files. Reinstallation appends the key again. No network call, private-key read, privilege escalation or SSH daemon startup.
verdicts.decision: On a machine, silently adding a package-supplied login key to the real user trust store is likely malicious persistence. The fixture name and fixture@localhost comment are acknowledged provenance clues but do not sandbox the write. Explicit authorized provisioning, possession of the corresponding private key and the actual SSH server deployment are unknown.

changes.reason: Declaration of an authorizedKeys-prefixed name proves neither a path nor persistence. Exact matcher, platform, types, size and notable severity retained; removed unsupported T1098.004 default.
Join/resolve text referencing authorized_keys is a path reference, not persistence. Exact matcher, scope and notable severity retained; removed unsupported T1098.004 default.

A write via authKeys/authorizedKeys-prefixed variables does not establish an SSH trust store. The benign key-export control writes a public key to /tmp/release.pub and formerly fired this suspicious rule and js-ssh-backdoor. Reuse the equivalent existing variable-write atom, require a nearby authorized_keys reference, retain all previous exclusions and suspicious severity. Description states co-occurrence rather than proven data flow.
Description now names the matched variable spelling; a variable name does not prove the target path.

coverage_limits: ltidisafe has one distinct hostile effect: host/user identity exfiltration. Existing file and npm-hook composites describe that same result. Network interfaces are enumerated but localip is never sent; commented uptime is not executed. No credential theft, persistence or arbitrary code execution invented to meet counts.

SSH fixture has one distinct hostile effect: install-time retained SSH login access (one hostile and one suspicious rule). Directory creation and 0700/0600 creation modes are notable mechanics of that effect. It does not escalate privileges, start sshd or exfiltrate a private key. No duplicate hostile added to meet minimum counts.
HTML has a remote encrypted routing service and a campaign policy redirect; final destination and credentials page are not in the archive. Identity of the operator and live remote state are unknown.
classifier_disagreement: Correct relocation leaves SSH hostile/suspicious findings intact but reduces aggregate ML probability from 0.99878716 (level 15000) to 0.99760056 (level -1, off calibrated grid). This is a classifier miss, not grounds to restore misplaced objective features. ltidisafe was and remains off the calibrated ML grid despite 0.9974145 aggregate probability and two hostile rules; its malicious test.js alone scores 0.0064587. HTML remains probability 0.98, level 25. No material attack rule coverage lost.
